name: Nazmul Haque Turja
intro: Hardware security, from design to verification.
bio: My PhD research in Electrical and Computer Engineering focuses on hardware security. I bring experience in GPU logic design and pre-silicon verification at Intel, alongside prior research in computer architecture and performance modeling.
now: Developing my PhD research in hardware security and exploring hardware design and verification using LLMs and AI agents. I will join the ECE Department at the University of Delaware as a Graduate Research Assistant on October 1, 2026.

research.title: Hardware security
research.summary: The focus of my PhD: understanding and improving the security of hardware systems.
research.body: My PhD in Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Delaware focuses on hardware security. I am developing this research direction with a foundation in hardware design, pre-silicon verification, and computer architecture.

research.title: Hardware design & verification
research.summary: Exploring LLMs and AI agents for hardware design and verification.
research.body: My ongoing research explores hardware design and verification using LLMs and AI agents. My prior work at Intel covered pre-silicon verification of GPUs, including Xe-Core ray tracing and texture sampling features, UVM-based validation, coverage closure, and regression debugging.

research.title: Architecture & performance
research.summary: Prior work in GPU performance prediction and CPU bottleneck analysis informs my hardware research.
research.body: My research includes machine learning for GPU basic block execution counts, reuse-distance and memory tracing tools for PPT-GPU, and CPI breakdown analysis for IBM Power9. This work draws on collaborations with Los Alamos National Laboratory and Sandia National Laboratories.

research.title: Embedded & connected systems
research.summary: Building practical systems that connect software, sensors, and hardware.
research.body: My earlier work explored secure IoT automation, embedded systems, and digital design. Projects include MQTT-based offline automation, a cache simulator, and a simulated 8-bit computer.
